title: Add invocation trajectory annotator and alert crossfade to reduce observability churn
author: Ananya Patel
description:
Motivation: We observe frequent alert churn for tail latency and token-cost alerts triggered by short-lived bursts that are related across many invocations. Root cause is noisy, overlapping signals where the same underlying workload shows up as multiple independent anomalies. This PR introduces an "invocation trajectory annotator" that groups related invocation signals into short-lived trajectories (by tenant, route, and prompt-fingerprint) and an "alert crossfade" policy that temporarily suppresses duplicate alerts for trajectories already owned by an active incident.

Summary of changes:
1) New trajectory annotator service and lightweight proto, integrated into the observability pipeline (ingest -> annotator -> alert-evaluator);
2) Trajectory tag propagation into traces/metrics/span labels so dashboards and digests can group events;
3) Crossfade alerting policy that reduces duplicate SLO alerts for 30s-5m windows based on trajectory affinity;
4) Dashboard panels to visualize trajectory heatmap and an incident impact view;
5) Config knobs exposed in console for trajectory TTL, affinity threshold, and crossfade window;
6) Safety: default opt-in disabled for existing tenants until rollout flags are set.

Commits:
- 1a2b3c4: introduce trajectory proto, serializer, and unit tests
- 2b3c4d5: implement annotator worker and affinity scoring
- 3c4d5e6: wire trajectory tags into trace/span enrichment paths
- 4d5e6f7: add alert crossfade policy and evaluation unit tests
- 5e6f7g8: console UI: add trajectory settings + dashboard panels
- 6f7g8h9: integration tests and e2e smoke for crossfade behavior

Files changed (high-level):
- obs/annotator/trajectory_service.go: new annotator and affinity scorer
- obs/annotator/proto/trajectory.proto: proto definition
- obs/pipeline/enricher.go: propagate trajectory tags into spans/metrics
- alerts/policy/crossfade.go: new crossfade policy and config
- console/src/routes/trajectory-settings.tsx: UI controls and rollout toggle
- console/dashboards/trajectory-heatmap.json: new dashboard panels
- tests/integration/trajectory_e2e_test.go: end-to-end validation
- docs/observability/trajectory.md: design notes and rollout plan
- charts/values.yaml: feature flag default off

Review notes:
- Affinity scoring uses a weighted combination of tenant, route, prompt-fingerprint, and prefetched-kv hit patterns. Threshold chosen conservatively to avoid over-grouping.
- Crossfade window default 60s with progressive rollouts to 5m for high-volume tenants.
- Observability metrics emitted: trajectory.created, trajectory.merged, crossfade.suppressed_alerts, crossfade.active_trajectories.
- Alerts impacted: token-latency-tail, token-cost-spike, per-route-slowpath.

Rollout plan: staged by tenant percent with feature-flag gating and synthetic replay to validate suppression rates.

CI summary: build: pass, unit-tests: pass (coverage +2% for annotator), integration-tests: pass in staging, lint: pass, dashboards-load: pass.

Review conversation (high level):
- Marcus Nguyen: "Can we avoid coupling trajectory TTL to cache TTL? I see potential mismatch during KV warmup." Author: "Good point. Decoupled the TTL; added explicit config and docs. See proto and charts change."
- Ellen Zhao: "Affinity threshold seems low for enterprise tenants; can we expose per-tenant override?" Author: "Exposed override in trajectory-settings and added validation in annotator."
- Diego Alvarez: "How do we audit suppressed alerts for oncall visibility?" Author: "Added crossfade.suppressed_alerts metric and a dashboard panel listing suppressed events for 24h; retention controlled by config."

Post-review changes: tightened affinity scoring (small penalty for cross-tenant matches), added unit tests for zero-affinity edgecases, added synthetic replay harness in tests/integration.

Performance impact: annotator service is CPU-light (single-threaded affinity scorer); measured end-to-end observability pipeline latency increase of ~4ms p95 in staging, within SLO.

Security and compliance: no plaintext customer data emitted; trajectory tag is a hashed fingerprint.

Docs and runbook: docs/observability/trajectory.md includes runbook for triage, how to interpret suppressed alert panels, and rollback steps.

Merge: squash and merged to main after approvals from Marcus and Ellen and green CI. Merge commit: 8f7a3c4.

Why unique: this PR focuses on grouping related invocation signals into trajectories and easing alert fatigue via a crossfade strategy rather than purely changing sampling or thresholds. It complements existing sampling and cohorting work by providing a transient ownership model for bursts.

Linked tickets: ENG-2371 (alert-churn reduction), ENG-2398 (trajectory design).

notes_for_oncall: If unexpected suppression observed, toggle feature flag off for affected tenant via console, consult docs/observability/trajectory.md runbook, and inspect crossfade.suppressed_alerts and trajectory.created metrics to verify traffic patterns.
